title: How is Adolf Hitler connected to Thomas the Tank Engine?
description: Six real photos connect Adolf Hitler to Thomas the Tank Engine, through Finland's wartime marshal, a future Finnish president, John F. Kennedy, a British prime minister and a Beatle.
hook: How is Adolf Hitler connected to Thomas the Tank Engine?
fun_fact: During Hitler's 1942 visit, a Finnish radio sound engineer secretly recorded the first 11 minutes of his talk with Mannerheim, the only known recording of Hitler speaking in an unofficial, everyday voice.
research_note: Instead of the usual Chamberlain or Franco exit, this chain leaves Hitler through Finland: a 1940 photo shows Mannerheim beside Kekkonen at a Helsinki athletics match, and the JFK Library has Kekkonen's 1961 state visit; a Finnish archive photo of Kekkonen with Harold Wilson exists, but its host blocks automated downloads, so the route runs through Kennedy.

links.line: In 1942, Hitler flew to Finland for the 75th birthday of its wartime commander, Marshal Mannerheim.

image.file: File:Famous spectators of athletics game Finland-Sweden-Germany, September 1940 in Helsinki.jpg

links.line: In 1940, Marshal Mannerheim watched athletics in Helsinki beside Urho Kekkonen, a future president of Finland.
In 1961, John F. Kennedy welcomed Finland's president, Urho Kekkonen, on a state visit to America.

image.file: File:President John F. Kennedy with Leader of the Labour Party of Great Britain, Harold Wilson.jpg

links.line: In 1963, John F. Kennedy met British Labour leader Harold Wilson at the White House.

image.credit: Terry O'Neill / Iconic Images (via Tristan's Gallery)

links.line: In 1964, Harold Wilson handed Ringo Starr and the Beatles a showbiz award in London.

image.credit: Thomas the Tank Engine & Friends publicity photo (via Thomas & Friends Wiki)

links.line: And in 1984, Ringo Starr became the first TV voice of Thomas the Tank Engine.
